correctness.rationale: The precise domain comprises all directed Euler circuits of the four-bit de Bruijn graph modulo rotation. Every tour induces exactly one of 2^16 bijective local incoming/outgoing pairings; the single-cycle predicate is necessary and sufficient. The fixed all-zero edge yields a unique root. An entirely separate unused-edge DFS yields the identical 2048 cycles. For each cycle, brute-force circular factors and the prefix-walk range yield the same discrepancy; full Parikh sets and independent sliding extrema yield the same peak Abelian complexity. All 2048 cases and eight cells are accounted for; reversal/complementation orbit counts and totals are exact. Limits: finite proof only at order 5, no extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: All-order existence of a minimum-discrepancy cycle establishes only the minimum value 5 here, not the 224 minimizing cycles, seven other frequency cells, joint Abelian peaks, or orbit allocation. value.rationale: Gabric–Sawada explicitly motivates the distribution of discrepancy across all de Bruijn sequences as a research direction. This complete 2048-cycle benchmark, at the first binary order with a sizable family, determines the exact chance of minimum discrepancy (224/2048), full joint local-balance/Abelian-complexity behavior and symmetry-reduced frequency classes; it shows Abelian peak does not determine circular discrepancy. The eight-cell distribution is neither a renaming of the known minimum theorem nor an arbitrary sample; it is an exact natural finite classification with a reproducible generator. Higher-order distributions remain open.
